sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: A tropical tree of humid forests in the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia, often near streams. It can reach about 15 m, sometimes taller.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: Its large white flowers are about 15–20 cm across. They are followed by a cluster of carpels enclosed by persistent, fleshy sepals; the whole structure is roughly 8–10 cm across.

sections.title: Food use
sections.text: The ripe, tart sepals are locally eaten fresh or cooked, including in fruit preparations. These reported uses apply to the sepals and do not establish that other parts are edible.
